**Wire verb `readers read-protein-groups` with `--paths-stdin`**: many inputs, one bridge process, one long table, per BULK.md.

# Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default | Unit | Range | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| wire `--paths-stdin` | `flag` | absent | — | — | Read MANY files: newline-delimited paths on stdin (blank lines ignored; a repeated path is a usage error). Exclusive with path; offset and limit are refused with it. |
| `threads` (wire `--threads`) | `int` | `1` | files | `>= 1, or -1 for one per core` | Files read at once. The output is byte-identical at any value (files are emitted in input order); 1 is the default because each file in flight is held whole in memory. |
| `on_error` (wire `--on-error`) | `string` | `fail` | — | `fail \| skip` | fail: the first unreadable input stops the batch with its usage or correctness error, the message starting 'Input &lt;i&gt; (&lt;path&gt;)'. skip: the failure goes in that input's files\[i\].error and the rest are read. skip with a single path is a usage error. |
| `out` (wire `--out`) | `path` | absent | — | — | Write the long table here, one file at a time in input order, so memory holds at most threads files. A batch that stops on an error deletes its partial table. Must differ from every input. |

# Returns

| Field | Type | Unit | Null? | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `file_count` | `int` | files | never | Paths given. |
| `read_count` | `int` | files | never | Files read. |
| `failed_count` | `int` | files | never | Files not read; non-zero only under on-error skip. |
| `record_count` | `int` | groups | never | Groups summed over the files read (BULK.md section 2). |
| `returned_count` | `int` | groups | never | Groups returned in columns, summed over the files; 0 when written to out. |
| `row_count` | `int` | rows | never | Rows in columns (more than returned\_count for a long view); 0 when written to out. |
| `on_error` | `string` | — | never | fail or skip, as requested. --threads is deliberately not echoed: the envelope is byte-identical at every thread count. |
| `columns` (wire `column_names`) | `string[]` | — | never | source\_index, source\_path, then the single-file columns. |
| `columns` | `table` | — | yes: the table was written to out instead | One long table: rows grouped by input in input order, each file's rows in its own order, whatever --threads is. |
| `output` | `object` | — | yes: out was not given | {path, format: "tsv", row\_count}; written one file at a time. |
| `files` | `object[]` | — | never | One per input, in input order: the per-file block (path, file\_type, reader, sample\_labels, record\_count, rows\_not\_read, retention\_time\_unit, caveats, column\_names, absent\_fields, failed\_fields, excluded\_fields, error). An unread input has error set and every fact it could not establish null or empty. |
